comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C7, C37, C38 regarding compensatory PRPH2 increase in Rom1-/- mice. Both evaluations support the findings based on mass spectrometry data, with peer reviewers explicitly praising the quantitative proteomic approach and rigor.

Perfect agreement on claims C8, C45-C47, C50-C51 regarding delayed disc enclosure in Rom1-/- mice. Both evaluations support the TEM findings with tannic acid staining, with peer reviewers highlighting the careful analysis and discovery of defects despite PRPH2 compensation.

Both address increased outer segment diameter (C9, C48) and absence of incisures (C10, C55) in Rom1-/- mice. OpenEval separates these into distinct results (R3 for diameter, R4 for incisures), while peer review groups them together as part of overall structural defects. Both evaluations are supportive.

OpenEval R4 addresses incisure absence (C10, C54-C57) with support but notes mechanistic speculation. Peer R3 includes C10 and C55 as part of broader structural phenotype characterization and is fully supportive without raising mechanistic concerns.

Both address rescue of Rom1-/- phenotypes by PRPH2 overexpression (C11, C77-C82). OpenEval finds the data well-supported and considers this a key finding. Peer review rates this as UNCERTAIN, noting missing quantitative data on molar ratios in PRPH2 overexpressing mice, which limits precision of conclusions about compensation mechanisms.

Both address disulfide bonding patterns (C64-C68, C74) and oligomerization. OpenEval R5 focuses on Western blot evidence for different disulfide patterns, while peer R5 encompasses broader biochemical assays including fractionation studies (C73, C75). Both are supportive, acknowledging the rigor of biochemical approaches.

OpenEval R6 addresses velocity sedimentation data (C71-C73, C75) showing oligomerization differences. Peer R5 includes C73 and C75 as part of broader biochemical characterization. Both evaluations support the findings, with OpenEval noting the causal link to disc enclosure is inferred rather than directly demonstrated.

Both address disc rim formation in RRCT mice (C12, C86, C89-C91). OpenEval notes limited rescue with severely disrupted outer segments, while peer review is fully supportive as part of comprehensive genetic analysis. OpenEval R8 also includes C94-C96 which peer R6 addresses.

OpenEval R9 addresses COS-7 cell reconstitution experiments (C92-C96) showing ROM1 can form complexes and traffic properly. Peer R6 includes C94-C96 as part of the RRCT mouse analysis. Both are supportive, though OpenEval notes in vitro limitations.

Both address disc rim formation in double mutant mice with PRPH2 C150S mutation (C97-C105). OpenEval notes rims can form but overall structure is severely impaired. Peer review supports this as evidence that PRPH2-ROM1 interactions are not required for disc enclosure. Both evaluations are supportive.

OpenEval R11 specifically addresses disc enclosure without intermolecular disulfide bonds (C104-C105) based on tannic acid staining. Peer R7 includes these claims as part of the broader double mutant analysis. Both evaluations support the finding that disulfide bonds are not required for enclosure.

Both address the main conclusion that ROM1 is functionally redundant to PRPH2 but requires excess PRPH2 for compensation (C123-C124). OpenEval finds this well-supported by comprehensive data. Peer reviewers explicitly endorse this conclusion as definitive and pushing the field forward. Strong agreement.

Both address morphometric quantification of Rom1-/- phenotypes (C40-C44 in OpenEval, C40-C41 plus statistical claims C128-C135 in peer review). Both evaluations support the quantitative approach, with peer reviewers specifically praising the unbiased quantitative analysis of EM images.

OpenEval R19 comprehensively addresses statistical methodology (C128-C146) as properly executed. Peer R9 includes subset of these statistical claims (C128-C135) as part of morphometric validation. Both evaluations support the statistical rigor and quantitative approach.

OpenEval R13 addresses mechanistic speculation about disc enclosure delay causing degeneration (C106-C110) and rates it as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these speculative mechanistic claims.

OpenEval R14 addresses differential compensation between ROM1 and PRPH2 knockout models (C111-C115), rating it as SUPPORTED based on literature comparisons. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these comparative claims.

OpenEval R15 addresses ROM1's unique contributions beyond redundancy (C116-C120), rating it as SUPPORTED by combined data but noting mechanisms remain partially speculative. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these interpretive claims about ROM1's unique features.

OpenEval R16 addresses conservation of total rim length (C121-C122), rating it as SUPPORTED by inference from diameter and tetraspanin data, though not directly measured. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this rim length conservation concept.

OpenEval R18 addresses therapeutic speculation (C125-C127) and rates it as UNCERTAIN, noting these are hypotheses for future work rather than demonstrated results. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses these therapeutic application claims.
